svg.text: Cog — Implemented Engine and Real-Client Roadmap
Stage 12 complete · main 77e8fb4 · Stage 14 real-client scope is proposed, not yet approved
CURRENT EXECUTABLE PATH — SINGLE-PROCESS MOCK CHAT CLIENT
Responses stream back through the same path; completed turns update the session tree and optional file store.
The current cog-cli process can also expose a Unix-socket IPC listener; rich external UI processes are not shipped.
IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED — STAGES 12.0–12.6 / ALL GATES DONE
Auto-save, structured logs, optional IPC listener
Boundary: mock endpoint only; no CLI resume yet
Session tree, forking, history, timing, billing
Store API: save / load / append / list / delete
Agent lifecycle, queued turns, tool-result identity
Headers: core · event · state · session · store · agent
Boundary: no real wire adapter or streamed tool calls
cog-net: HTTP/1.1 streaming, stalls, retry, cancel
Explicit boundary: cog-net parses http:// only
Spawn, stop, kill, health, placement, shutdown
Real crash/reap and cross-core IPC scenarios
Implemented library + owned aux_core test fixtures
cog-orchestrator owns fixture PIDs; IPC fabric uses real Unix domain sockets
Verified: crash/reap · recovery primitives · session routing · fan-out/fan-in · bounded shutdown
These are executable test fixtures, not a separate shipped multi-process chat product.
Real-provider work must preserve the single-threaded core and caller-owned lifecycle contracts.
Choose TLS/HTTP and JSON integration through measured PoCs
Test fragmented SSE, cancellation, and sanitized wire fixtures
Then amend headers and trace real-client scenarios before code
B · Secure HTTPS transport + secret handling
TLS certificate, hostname, and SNI verification
Secret redaction across logs, errors, diagnostics, and sessions
Generic error metadata instead of mock-specific CLI inspection
Usage / finish metadata and structured content deltas
Stable tool-call identities, cancellation, and ownership rules
D · Real provider adapter + JSON / SSE codec
OpenAI-compatible HTTPS API proposed as the first protocol
Request serialization + incremental SSE response decoding
External LLM service: model errors, rate limits, usage, streaming
CLI / environment / config-file loading with clear precedence
Session resume / list / fork / delete and provider/model selection
Interactive slash commands, actionable errors, safe shutdown
F · Safe tool-conversation loop — following release
Accumulate streamed calls and return stable tool results
Confirmation, allowlists, output limits, and bounded model rounds
Preserve complete tool-call/result history in the session tree
Local TLS/wire tests by default; opt-in live-provider matrix
Sanitizers, credential-safety audit, install and user documentation
core.h, event.h, session.h, session_store.h, agent.h, tool.h, …
cog_obs_t · static field/sink tables · connection diagnostics
Mock REPL done; real UX needed
Evidence: 61/61 tests · 21/21 scenario-labeled tests · GCC + Clang Werror · ASan/UBSan/LSan · separate TSan · install/export smoke
Green describes merged functionality, not production readiness for real providers. Yellow blocks require blueprint confirmation, contracts, scenarios, implementation, and review.
Source of truth: docs/DESIGN.md · docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STRATEGY.md · docs/IMPLEMENTATION_WBS.md · merged Stage 12 tickets and verification
